name: Source Lock Release Skips An Empty Callback Queue

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Source Lock Release Skips An Empty Callback Queue Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

Releasing a `SourceLock` (every source edit and read, and every live-group member operation) always locks the `release_callbacks` mutex to take an almost always empty queue. An atomic flag set after a callback is queued and swapped off before the queue is taken lets a release skip that lock; `on_next_release` already takes the lock afterwards when it is free, so a callback queued while another thread releases is still run by a later release.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** atomic pending flag in front of the release-callback queue.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/collections/source_lock.rs` (`on_next_release`, `run_release_callbacks`, the struct).
**Forbidden in this experiment:** HELD tracking, release hook, fences elsewhere.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Focused tests: `collections::tests::{source_lock_policy,source_commit_order,suspension_versions,connect_late_delivery,sources,grouping_tree_switching}` and full lib; clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` cache/list updates, `live_group`, `operator_updates` (group), `tree` vs base. Pass: live-group load or cache-hot/update-* >=5% faster; nothing slower >10% on rerun.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

One mutex round trip less per source lock release.
